title: api: schema versioning, deprecations, beta headers, and backcompat shims for OpenAI-compat endpoints
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: stabilize our public API surface while enabling iterative schema changes. This PR implements a schema versioning/compatibility layer for OpenAI-compatible endpoints and introduces backward-compatibility shims and opt-in beta headers. It also includes fixes to streaming behavior for function/tool-calling and structured-output paths so older clients keep working during the rollout.

What changed: 
- Add `Redwood-Schema-Version` header handling (server and validation) and a request/response `schema_version` negotiation flow for OpenAI-compat endpoints so clients can opt into newer shapes.
- Introduce deprecation warnings returned in response headers (`Redwood-Deprecation-Warning`) and a mapped `X-OpenAI-Deprecation` header for compatibility.
- Implement lightweight backcompat shims that transform older request shapes into the v2 internal canonical shape: tool/function-calling meta, structured-output `components` -> `content` mapping, streaming frame compatibility.
- Stabilize streaming code paths used by function-calling and structured output: ensure chunk metadata (tool_call, end_of_stream, chunk_index) is preserved and consistent across schema versions.
- Update OpenAI compatibility adapter to respect schema version header and fall back gracefully when omitted (defaults to legacy compatibility mode).
- Add comprehensive unit + integration tests and docs + migration notes in docs/api/versioning.md and redwood-docs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Schema negotiation headers and validation
- [x] Backcompat transformation layer for incoming requests
- [x] Outgoing response deprecation headers
- [x] Streaming frame stabilization for tool/function-calling
- [x] Tests (unit + integration streaming)
- [x] Docs and migration guide

Notes on rollout: This is behind the feature flag `api.schema_versioning` and default behavior is unchanged. We will flip default to opt-in beta header acceptance after staged rollout and telemetry observation.

Impact: Users who set `Redwood-Schema-Version: 2` will get the new v2 request/response shapes (structured-output as `components` object, stricter tool invocation metadata). Older clients without headers will continue to work due to shims but will receive deprecation warnings. Breaking changes are feature-gated and documented.
